post_title: How many AIS-visible commercial ship crossings of the Strait of Hormuz will hormuz.now record for 26 November 2026?

question.title: How many AIS-visible commercial ship crossings of the Strait of Hormuz will hormuz.now record for 26 November 2026?
question.description:
Status as of 13 November 2026, Day 259 of the Strait of Hormuz crisis. The strait has been effectively closed to normal commercial traffic since 28 February 2026, when Iran began targeting ships transiting without its authorisation; the United States responded with a naval blockade of Iranian ports and has been helping tankers cross. Attempts to reopen the waterway have repeatedly stalled — Iran has said the strait will never return to its pre-war status — and attacks continue: on 12 November 2026 Iran's armed forces reported fires aboard four tankers in the strait. The Joint Maritime Information Center threat level is reported as 'severe', and war-risk insurance premiums at 3–10% of hull value.

Before the crisis the strait carried about 84.8 commercial transits a day (IMF PortWatch daily-transit-call average for the 365 days to 27 February 2026, roughly 47.6 of them tankers). Current traffic is roughly 8% of that. hormuz.now, which counts AIS-visible commercial ships of 80 m or more crossing its counting line once per direction, reports a 7-day average of 6.4 crossings a day, 45 crossings in the past 7 days (17 tankers, no LNG or LPG carriers) and 188 crossings over the past 30 days. Its most recent complete daily totals are 13 (6 November), 5 (7 November), 5 (8 November), 4 (11 November) and 6 (12 November), with 4 recorded so far on 13 November — a volatile series in which a single day can be two or three times another.

Counters differ materially in both level and timing, which is why this question fixes one. IMF PortWatch's satellite-AIS 'daily transit calls' counted 3 transits on 8 November (7-day average 3.9) and monthly averages of 3.2 in March 2026 and 3.8 in October 2026 — roughly half of hormuz.now's figures — but PortWatch publishes only weekly (Tuesdays, ~09:00 ET) and would not report 26 November until early December, after this question resolves. Windward, whose counts include AIS-dark vessels, recorded 10 transits on 12 November, 8 of them dark. UKMTO's weekly report counted 170 outbound and 155 inbound transits in the week to about 10 November, an implied ~46 a day. Even within hormuz.now, published figures for the same day can disagree: the 11 November briefing email said 8 ships crossed, while the archive page for 11 November shows 4 commercial crossings — hence this question resolves off the date-specific archive page.

Forecasting considerations: the outcome depends on whether the shooting war and the mutual interdiction regime around the strait continue at the current tempo, whether the large queue of vessels waiting on the Gulf of Oman side (hundreds at anchor at times) is cleared or further deferred, and whether any reopening, new closure or major attack lands inside the specific 24-hour window of 26 November 2026.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the number displayed as the headline 'commercial crossings' count on hormuz.now's daily archive page for 26 November 2026, https://hormuz.now/traffic/2026-11-26 (the same daily totals are listed at https://hormuz.now/data). The snapshot is the value shown on that page at 2026-11-27 12:00 UTC; any later revision of the figure is ignored. That archive page is authoritative: where it disagrees with hormuz.now's news page, status page or daily briefing email — which have at times reported different numbers for the same day — the archive page governs. For example, if the page shows '6 commercial crossings', the question resolves to 6. If the page is not yet showing a complete-day figure at the snapshot time, the first complete-day figure subsequently shown on that page is used (and later revisions still ignored). If hormuz.now publishes no count for 26 November 2026 at all, the question is annulled.
question.fine_print: The counted figure is hormuz.now's own AIS-based 'commercial crossings' total — AIS-visible commercial ships (cargo ships and tankers of 80 m or more) crossing its counting line, counted once per direction — as defined at https://hormuz.now/methodology. Small-craft crossings are excluded, and the inbound/outbound and tanker sub-figures are not used. Only crossings occurring between 00:00 and 23:59 UTC on 26 November 2026 count. A figure presented as an in-progress count for the day (e.g. 'so far today') is not a complete-day figure.
